column1: # case_id<TAB>config_id, `*` or `-`<TAB>cannot-validate:<reason prefix><TAB>reason
# Only cannot-validate records can be classified: the quick tier has NO baseline, so a
# discrepancy or representation violation always fails. Classifying a record never
# makes its configuration count as validated; it only says why it was not.
# case_id is file#<case name>#<ordinal among same-named cases in that file>
# (`%`, `#`, `|`, tab in the name are %-escaped). The reason prefix must match the
# record's first item on whole `:` segments; entries below use the whole item minus
# its `@offset`, so each one pins the reason, the node type it stopped at and, for
# unsupported-type and one-reading, the refused node's host (`: host <parent>:<slot>`).
# `*` expands to every predicted configuration of the case; `-` is the one record of
# an input whose directives do not resolve. An entry (or `*` expansion) that matches
# no record is STALE and fails the run with exit 1.
# Every reason starts with its category (fixtures.load_classes enforces all of this):
#   negative:        the input is invalid AL on purpose. Needs `evidence:`.
#   invalid-config:  this one configuration's text is not valid AL on its own; the
#                    fixture pins the tree of the configuration(s) that are. Needs `evidence:`.
#   debt(<owner>):   verification debt with the roadmap item that removes it. debt(C1):
#                    the oracle has no lowering for this shape yet, each reason naming the
#                    missing piece. A grammar gap (valid AL the grammar gets wrong) is
#                    debt(<row>) too; the last one, debt(B3), was closed 2026-10-01.
#                    Adding a handler turns its entry stale, which records the fix.
# Evidence is `evidence: alc_probe <case .al>` (a tools/alc_probe/cases file that
# `python -m tools.alc_probe run tools/alc_probe/cases --check` keeps honest; the loader
# requires its `expect:` to be a reject for every configuration the entry covers) or
# `evidence: probe_alc <name>` (a raw compile recorded in tools/config_oracle/probe_alc.py
# PROBES, kept honest by `python -m tools.config_oracle.probe_alc --check`; the loader
# requires the name to exist and to expect a reject, and refuses it for `*`) or
# `evidence: alc manual, <when>` for inputs alc_probe cannot run (its resolver refuses
# them). The probe's `// Fixture <case_id>` line must name this entry's case. The probe
# body is a self-contained, hand-stubbed copy of the fixture: nothing detects drift
# between the two, so re-probe when a fixture's #if structure changes.
# A `*` negative must cite an alc_probe case: `*` claims every configuration is
# rejected, and a manual note cannot be checked for that (the F1 finding of the A3
# review: a `*` negative covered a configuration alc accepts).
